note: PASS. Follows the batch_260 bfi_goldberg_1992_agreeableness convention (as reused in batch_261), re-verified for this table rather than copied. SOURCE: openpsychometrics.org/_rawdata/BIG5.zip re-downloaded 2026-09-19, sha256 67953298d75d3279d0486e7f4ec0195efc26a9e790b15e511cbcf4551751ba53 (identical to batch_260/261); BIG5/codebook.txt keys data.csv columns O1..O10 to verbatim statements (tab-separated, CRLF; trailing CR stripped). MAPPING (data_labels, core-model pattern 1): data/bfi_goldberg_1992.r selects O_items <- paste0("O",1:10) BY NAME and pivots names_to="item", so each IRW code IS the source column name -- no positional step; codebook level, 10/10 codes matched; live item set via irw_table_sets = O1..O10, resp {1..5}, 197,190 rows = 19,719 persons x 10. item_text copied verbatim from the codebook including its leading "I " and final period (e.g. O1 "I have a rich vocabulary.", O10 "I am full of ideas."). ANCHORS: codebook sentence "rated on a five point scale where 1=Disagree, 3=Neutral, 5=Agree (0=missed)" -> resp 1/3/5 labelled, resp 2 and 4 left blank (unlabelled, not padded); the script sets 0=missed to NA, hence live resp set 1-5. INSTRUCTIONS: first sentence of the Procedure paragraph of https://openpsychometrics.org/tests/IPIP-BFFM/ (fetched 2026-09-19, page sha256 b2287c9935c0e76b4e1687df857c7ec5b7b17889ee56ba1f26c197a847af6119 -- differs from earlier fetches, but the Procedure sentence is identical; page reads "Updated: 2 August 2019"); data collected c.2012 per the codebook, so this is the current landing-page wording, not a confirmed 2012 screen; "It takes most people 3-8 minutes to complete." omitted as not an instruction. STEP 3b: dictionary Description "Big Five Inventory: Openness to Experience" and the bfi_ table name are wrong about the instrument -- the live items are the 10-item Factor V scale of the 50-item IPIP Big-Five Factor Markers (Goldberg 1992), NOT the BFI-44; matched word for word (10/10, modulo the codebook adding the subject "I " and conjugating Am->am) against https://ipip.ori.org/newBigFive5broadKey.htm (fetched 2026-09-19, sha256 8577862772802903db4330c5a2178bd3948894fe86b82909865bb9b5f17411f9). IPIP names that factor "Intellect or Imagination", not Openness to Experience; the codebook and table label the same items O1-O10 as openness, and the instrument field names both labels. IPIP keying: + keyed rich vocabulary (O1), vivid imagination (O3), excellent ideas (O5), quick to understand things (O7), use difficult words (O8), spend time reflecting on things (O9), full of ideas (O10); - keyed difficulty understanding abstract ideas (O2), not interested in abstract ideas (O4), do not have a good imagination (O6). RIGHTS: instrument_rights_register.csv IPIP row (verdict ship, batch_140) applied, not re-derived; ipip.ori.org home page re-read 2026-09-19 (sha256 45d41652bdf7a434973b8501051272e2e8b764f588629fed96f22116d184cd0e): "The items and scales are in the public domain, which means that one can copy, edit, translate, or use them for any purpose without asking permission and without paying a fee." The BFI-44 block does not apply (different instrument). The test page sentence "Your use of this tool should be for educational or entertainment purposes only ... come with no guarantee of accuracy or fitness for a particular purpose" is a fitness disclaimer about the online tool, reserving no right over the public-domain wording, so it does not block. SANITY (not required for data_labels): in the local data.csv (0 set to NA, as the script does) the - keyed O2/O4/O6 have means 2.1/2.1/1.8 vs 3.2-4.1 for the rest and correlate -0.33/-0.23/-0.21 with O1 while the + keyed O3/O5/O7/O8/O9/O10 correlate +0.20..+0.63, so the stored data are raw (unreversed) and the Disagree..Agree direction holds; every item uses all 5 levels; local non-missing n = 19718 for all 10 items.
public_note: The dictionary calls this table the Big Five Inventory, but its items are the IPIP Big-Five Factor Markers (Goldberg, 1992) Intellect or Imagination scale, coded here as Openness to Experience (items O2, O4 and O6 are reverse-keyed and stored unreversed), administered by the Open-Source Psychometrics Project, not the BFI-44.

Instructions and the 10-point ladder (1 Never .. 10 Several times a day) transcribed from the codebook's Coding section. Rights: the Lifestyle Survey is the study team's own behaviour-frequency list, published in the study's OSF project rf9k8 under CC BY-SA 4.0 (read from api.osf.io/v2/nodes/rf9k8 license embed). source_ref: OSF rf9k8 (CC BY-SA 4.0) Study 2/Data/perceiver_ratings_raw_data.csv (osf.io/download/zhynf) header row; APA supplement pspp0000545.docx Supporting Text H (survey printout); Talaifar, Jordan, Gosling & Harari (2025) JPSP 129(1):152-180, doi:10.1037/pspp0000545
note: WORDS: item_text is the Qualtrics header-row label (row 2) of each rated column in the study's own deposited export perceiver_ratings_raw_data.csv (OSF rf9k8 'Study 2 - Perceived Lifestyle Polarization/Data', https://osf.io/download/zhynf/, sha256 8365d20a...0e), with the Qualtrics question-name prefix ('communication1 - ' etc.) stripped; all 61 labels were cross-checked character-for-character (after whitespace/NBSP normalisation) against the survey printout in Supporting Text H of the APA supplement (supp.apa.org/psycarticles/supplemental/pspp0000545/pspp0000545.docx, sha256 8af3cba5...1e) -- 61/61 identical. instructions = the introduction block's 'IMPORTANT INSTRUCTIONS' text (whole-table framing); section_prompt = each domain block's descriptive text (comm_des/leis_des/work_des/move_des), kept per section because the wording differs across blocks ('undergraduate students at UT Austin' vs 'UT Austin students' vs 'students'). Slider anchors -1/0/1 are the printout's labels 'Liberals always do this more' / 'Conservatives and liberals do this equally' / 'Conservatives always do this more' (the paper text quotes the same three). MAPPING: IRW codes are NOT the source column names -- data/talaifar_2025_lifestyle_polarization.py renames Qualtrics columns (communication1_1 ...) to Study 1 sensing/EMA variable names (smsinnum ...) via a hand-written dict, which reproduces the authors' own rename in their deposited correlational_categorical_accuracy.R 61/61. Because the rename is neither identity nor number-preserving, it was verified: every live item's per-respondent (id, resp) vector matches exactly one of the 61 source columns, the dict's (61/61), see verify_talaifar_2025_study2_plp.R. DEVIATIONS, all deliberate: (1) whitespace/NBSP collapsed and multi-line block text joined with single spaces; (2) source typos kept verbatim ('Who spending more time at home during the day?', 'Ratings of 0 indicates'); (3) the slider's numeric tick marks (-1, -.8, ..., 1) are a scale ruler, not labels, so resp -0.99..0.99 except 0 ship with option_text blank, not padded; each item carries a row for every resp level its own respondents used plus the three anchor levels -1/0/1 (4,814 rows; union = all 201 live levels -1..1 by 0.01) -- unused intermediate slider positions are omitted rather than emitted as 12,261 mostly-empty rows (an 18 MB file); (4) attention check communication1_11 ('Slide the scale to .5 ...') is not an IRW item and is not shipped; (5) section_id follows the administered Qualtrics block, so loc_friendshouse (leisure1_9) sits in the leisure section although the IRW itemcov_domain / authors' analysis category calls it social. RIGHTS: the items are the study's own bespoke questions (no published instrument); deposit CC BY-SA 4.0 (OSF rf9k8 node licence), article published CC BY per the APA supplement page. No reserved right to quote; nothing in instrument_rights_register.csv. SOURCE-RECORD DEFECT: the IRW dictionary DOI 10.1037/pspp0000548 resolves (Crossref) to a different article ('Evaluating the psychological and social nature of actual and perceived liking gaps'); the correct DOI is 10.1037/pspp0000545.
public_note: Item codes are the names of the Study 1 sensing/EMA variables each question was matched to by the authors (e.g. 'maxdistance' is the question 'Who travels a further total distance?'), so read the item_text, not the code, for what respondents rated; ratings run from -1 (liberals always do this more) to 1 (conservatives always do this more).
